grammar.title: Present Perfect vs Past Simple
grammar.explanation:
We use the **present perfect** for past actions with a result now. We use the **past simple** for finished actions at a finished time.

Form the **present perfect** with **have** or **has** + past participle. Form the **past simple** with the past form of the verb.

Use the **present perfect** with **just**, **already**, **yet**, and **ever**. Use the **past simple** with **yesterday**, **last week**, and **in 2020**.

Compare: **I have bought** a new outfit means it is new for you now. **I bought** an outfit yesterday tells you when it happened.

Do not use the **present perfect** with a finished time. Say **I saw a trendy jacket yesterday**, not **I have seen a trendy jacket yesterday**.
examples: *I have bought* a new outfit for the party. (recent action, result now)
*She has visited* a vintage shop in town. (experience, no time given)
*We bought* this fabric last week. (finished time)
*He has already chosen* a stylish accessory. (already + present perfect)
*They met* a tailor in the market yesterday. (finished time)
*Have you ever worn* a trendy pattern like this? (ever + present perfect)
